comments.author: @SkiBumMSP
comments.text: That one at 5:00 minutes in!  She can go and pound sand!  No, I do NOT want to live beyond my means.  Living within my means is not in the least bit way making my life any less satisfactory.  In fact, I find my life to be a lot more satisfactory by living well within my means.  That means I have a huge savings thus pretty much giving me insurance if anything does go south.  For example, my water heater died last year and had to get it replace - paid for cash out of emergency savings.  No only that, but had a bout with colon cancer and thankfully my health insurance and HSA covered that!  That also means that I have absolutely no debt, thus I don't have to worry about cars being repossessed (both vehicles paid for), house being foreclosed (both houses completely paid for - my main residence and a tiny place in the mountains at the ski resort), no credit card late fees and penalty rates, etc.  Living within my means mean that I have the financial security and stability that gives me the freedom to whatever I want with the extra money that I do have.  What I mean by "extra money" is whatever I have left over after both the bills AND the allotment for investments/retirement funds are paid.   Yes, I do like to take a trip skiing somewhere every year.  Yes, I do like to dabble in high-end audio.  Yes, I do have season tickets to the local baseball team.  Yes, I do like to go to concerts (Friggan $360 for Rush!  🤨), but I am doing all that WITHING MY MEANS and thus can afford it.  And yes, I did eventually replenish the money I took out for the water heater repair back to the emergency fund.  So yeah, any of those imbeciles that say we should just all blow it all and "enjoy life" can go stuff it, like as though that money is going to somehow magically appear.
